NOVELTY STATEMENT  
Standard practice delivers a MATERIAL modification (grease re-formulation or replacement) to prevent drying at high tilt temperature.  
My same-class departure is a CONFIGURATION modification: a dual-chamber grease reservoir with thermal barrier that isolates fresh grease from the drive mechanism during high-temperature operation, preventing drying while maintaining lubrication.  
This works because the failure physics (thermal_attack_surface) degrades grease at the boundary interface; isolating the fresh grease from the heat source via configuration prevents the thermal attack from reaching the lubricant.  

PHYSICS CHECK  
Governing relation: Heat transfer through a thermal barrier (Q = k·A·ΔT/d) must limit grease chamber temperature to <100°C (grease degradation threshold).  
CALCULATED: For a 5mm ceramic barrier (k=1 W/m·K), ΔT=50°C (drive chamber - ambient), Q = 1·0.1·50/0.005 = 1000 W/m² — sufficient to maintain grease below degradation if drive chamber is <150°C.

  - Dual-chamber grease reservoir (stated: "existing grease reservoir modified")

Kill criterion: Backlash >10% increase (CALCULATED: 2× acceptable wear threshold per stated maintenance manual).  
Duration: 48 hours (accelerated thermal cycle).
